documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Students
documents.stance_why: The students' page gives no AI rule itself: 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment' and 'Your instructors will explain what is permitted'. The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Provost message to students on the updated Academic Integrity Policy S26-10. It says AI rules vary by course, tells students to ask when unsure, lists AI-literacy resources, and explains how integrity concerns and appeals work.

units.why: The provost says the revised policy was written because of 'the growing use of artificial intelligence'; this is an institution-level preamble stating purpose, so P56 and informs, not a rule on student behavior.
units.anchor: responds to changes in teaching, learning, and technology, including the growing use of artificial intelligence

units.why: 'Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment' leaves the rule to each course, so P04 (instructor or assignment sets the rule) and informs.
units.anchor: Rules for using AI may vary by course and assignment.

units.why: 'Your instructors will explain what is permitted, so please read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully' tells students where to find the AI rules. No type covers a student duty to read the syllabus (P09 binds instructors), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: please read your syllabus and assignment instructions carefully
units.uncovered_note: Students are told to read the syllabus and assignment instructions carefully to learn the AI rules.

units.why: 'If you are unsure whether you may use an AI tool ... ask your instructor before submitting your work' is the ask-first rule, P10, with should.
units.anchor: ask your instructor before submitting your work

units.why: 'how you should acknowledge its use' signals that acknowledgment of AI is decided per course; closest is P24 but the passage only names acknowledgment as something to ask about, not a requirement.
units.anchor: how you should acknowledge its use
units.policy: Students who are unsure how to acknowledge AI use ask their instructor before submitting work.
units.fit_note: Acknowledgment is not required outright; the passage only says to ask the instructor how to acknowledge AI use.

units.why: The provost says SJSU 'provides a number of resources to help students navigate the ethical use of generative and agentic AI tools', including the AI Writer's Toolbox; institutional AI-literacy resources for students are P70, informs.
units.anchor: provides a number of resources to help students navigate the ethical
units.policy: SJSU provides resources, including the AI Writer's Toolbox, to help students navigate the ethical use of generative and agentic AI tools.

units.why: 'where you can also book tutoring appointments' sends students to the Writing Center, human help alongside AI tools, so P72.
units.anchor: where you can also book tutoring appointments
units.policy: Students can book tutoring appointments at the SJSU Writing Center, which helped build the AI Writer's Toolbox.

units.why: Students 'have access to a course on AI Literacy Essentials' designed by CFETI; a course offered to students is P70.
units.anchor: Students also have access to a course on
units.policy: Students have access to a course on AI Literacy Essentials designed by the Center for Excellence and Teaching Innovation.

units.why: 'The SJSU Career Center also has numerous training opportunities' to navigate responsible AI use; training for students is P70.
units.anchor: numerous training opportunities for students
units.policy: The SJSU Career Center offers training opportunities that help students navigate the ethical and responsible use of AI tools.

units.why: 'Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you and explain any proposed academic sanction before reporting' is talk-before-escalating, P57, directed at instructors.
units.anchor: Instructors are expected to discuss the concern with you

units.why: 'Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline' sets a procedural deadline for integrity reports. It falls under handling misconduct through integrity processes (P36), but only the deadline is stated.
units.anchor: Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline
units.fit_note: States only the reporting deadline for integrity concerns, not that AI misuse is misconduct.

units.why: 'You also have the right to appeal' an academic sanction reviewed by the ADRRC gives accused students a way to respond, P64, with permit.
units.anchor: You also have the right to appeal
units.frag_end: opportunity for you to be heard.

units.why: 'If you do your own work, follow your instructor's directions' says students must submit their own work; closest is P29, though the passage is general integrity, not AI-specific.
units.anchor: If you do your own work, follow your instructor

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Academic Senate
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy (S26-10) - Campus Updates for Faculty
documents.stance_why: The faculty page says 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses', and sets only process rules (reporting, detector evidence), so it delegates the stance.
documents.summary: Provost message to faculty on S26-10. Instructors set and communicate AI rules, report sanctions to SCED on set timelines, use only approved detectors, and may not sanction on detector output alone.

units.why: The provost cites 'valid questions about the efficacy and limitations of AI detection technologies' as a reason for the revision; that is a statement that detectors are unreliable, P39, informs.
units.anchor: valid questions about the efficacy and limitations of AI detection technologies

units.why: 'you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development (SCED)' and no sanction 'without submitting an Academic Integrity Reporting Form' is a mandatory process step for misconduct, closest P36; it is not AI-specific.
units.anchor: an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting
units.policy: Instructors who impose an academic sanction must report the matter to SCED, and a sanction may not be imposed without an Academic Integrity Reporting Form.
units.fit_note: Mandatory reporting procedure for any integrity violation; the passage does not mention AI.

units.why: Faculty are 'expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days' of a suspected incident; this is talking with the student before escalation, P57.
units.anchor: expected to communicate and confer with the student within 10 working days
units.fit_note: Adds a 10-working-day deadline and a no-later-than-grade-release limit.

units.why: The report 'must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident' is a deadline for the misconduct report; P36 is nearest, as no type covers report timing.
units.anchor: must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident
units.policy: Reports, including supporting documentation and communications with the student, must be submitted to SCED within 15 working days of the incident.
units.fit_note: Only the 15-working-day reporting deadline and required documentation.

units.why: 'Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools in their courses' puts the decision with the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty remain responsible for determining whether and how students may use AI tools

units.why: 'Make sure to communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions' tells instructors to put AI expectations in syllabi, P09; the wording is an exhortation, so should.
units.anchor: communicate those expectations clearly in your syllabi and assignment instructions

units.why: 'you may want to use SJSU's AI Policy Builder' points instructors to a support tool for crafting a course AI policy, P63 (support for faculty).
units.anchor: you may want to use SJSU
units.policy: Instructors may use SJSU's AI Policy Builder to craft an AI policy for their course.
units.fit_note: A policy-drafting tool rather than workshops or consultations.

units.why: 'Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university. At SJSU, you have access to Turnitin' restricts instructors to approved detectors, P40 for use of detection tools.
units.anchor: Faculty may only use detection services approved by the university.
units.policy: Faculty may only use AI-detection services approved by the university; at SJSU, Turnitin is available.
units.fit_note: Limits which detectors may be used (approved only) rather than directing use of them.

units.why: Detection tools 'must, however, be approached with great caution' because they 'have become less effective over time' and give false positives; this is a warning on detector unreliability, P39.
units.anchor: must, however, be approached with great caution as they have become less effective

units.why: Detection reports 'cannot serve as the sole basis for imposing an academic sanction' sets an evidence standard for AI misuse findings, P69 rather than P39, since detectors are still allowed alongside other evidence.
units.anchor: alongside other evidence. They cannot serve as the sole basis

units.why: 'Other evidence may include documentation that the submitted assignment represents a significant or noteworthy change from the student's previous work' lists kinds of evidence to weigh, P69.
units.anchor: documentation that the submitted assignment represents a significant or noteworthy change

units.why: S26-10 'introduces a sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity of a violation'; sanctions are stated in advance, nearest P37, though they are recommendations and not specific penalties here.
units.anchor: sanctioning matrix with recommended sanctions based on the nature and severity
units.fit_note: Recommended sanctions in a matrix; specific penalties are not named in this text and the matrix is not AI-specific.

units.why: 'The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment' keeps the sanction a faculty decision; it qualifies P37 and is not a concrete penalty.
units.anchor: The matrix is a guide, not a substitute for faculty judgment.
units.fit_note: Says the sanctions are advisory and discretionary, not stated penalties.

units.why: 'CFETI can provide you with relevant AI Pedagogical Resources' and offers consultations; this is faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: The Center offers in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty members
units.policy: CFETI provides AI Pedagogical Resources and in-person and Zoom consultations for individual faculty, programs and departments.

units.why: CFETI consultations help faculty 'better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin'; faculty support on detector limits, P63.
units.anchor: better understand the effectiveness, limits, and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin
units.policy: CFETI consultations can help faculty understand the effectiveness, limits and drawbacks of tools such as Turnitin.

units.why: A CFETI workshop on 'Turnitin Clarity' that shows 'drafting history' of student writing is a faculty training item (P63) that also relates to process evidence (P40); P63 chosen since the passage is about the workshop, not a rule to use process evidence.
units.anchor: workshop that introduces faculty to Turnitin Clarity
units.policy: CFETI hosts a workshop introducing faculty to Turnitin Clarity, a tool that focuses on the student's writing process and reveals drafting history, as part of the Turnitin Clarity Pilot Project.
units.fit_note: Also describes a pilot of a process-evidence tool (P40).

units.why: 'please review the revised policy, update your course materials as needed' asks instructors to revise course materials after the policy change; nearest P09, partial.
units.anchor: update your course materials as needed
units.fit_note: Asks instructors to update course materials generally, not specifically to add an AI statement.

units.why: 'Additional resources and training on S26-10 and Academic Integrity, will become available in the coming weeks' commits the university to further faculty training, P63.
units.anchor: Additional resources and training on S26-10 and Academic Integrity

documents.title: Developing a Generative AI Syllabus Policy
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment'; the university sets no stance of its own and only requires a stated policy, so delegates.
documents.summary: Library guide for faculty on writing a generative AI syllabus policy. It restates S26-10's duty to state an AI policy, points to the AI Policy Builder, AI Pedagogical Resources and SAID.

units.why: 'requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence ... in the syllabus' is a mandatory AI statement, P09, must.
units.anchor: requires instructors to communicate their course policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence

units.why: 'Faculty should clearly explain whether and how generative AI may be used in their course' sets the content of the statement, including 'expectations for acknowledgment or citation'; P09 with should.
units.anchor: Faculty should clearly explain whether and how generative AI may be used

units.why: The AI Policy Builder lets faculty 'create or customize a syllabus statement using approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use'; a policy-drafting tool for faculty, P63, with an option set like P05.
units.anchor: approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use
units.policy: CFETI's SJSU AI Policy Builder helps faculty create or customize a syllabus statement using approaches that allow, restrict, or prohibit generative AI use.
units.fit_note: Names three approaches (allow, restrict, prohibit) but not defined tiers.

units.why: 'AI Pedagogical Resources' give 'guidance for incorporating, limiting, or addressing AI use in teaching'; faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Guidance for incorporating, limiting, or addressing AI use in teaching and coursework.

units.why: SAID is 'a resource faculty can use to help students document how they used AI'; supports student disclosure, closest P24, but it is an optional resource.
units.anchor: help students document how they used AI in their coursework
units.policy: Faculty can use SAID (Student AI Disclosure) to help students document how they used AI in their coursework.
units.fit_note: An optional disclosure resource for faculty, not a requirement on students.

units.why: 'Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI depending on the course and assignment' leaves the decision per course and assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty may allow, restrict, or prohibit the use of generative AI

units.why: 'communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions' requires AI expectations at both course and assignment level, P09, should.
units.anchor: communicate expectations clearly in both the syllabus and assignment instructions

notes: Coder B. Only three university-layer documents are included; no computing-level or school-level document in the collect file. The students and faculty pages are provost summaries of Academic Integrity Policy S26-10; the full policy PDF was not in the collected text, so its own wording is not coded. Several enforcement-procedure units are not AI-specific and carry fit notes.
